content.text:
Paint a book cover. Portrait, 1600 by 2560 pixels.

The scene: a kitchen table late in the evening, seen from a little above.
On the left side of the table sits a tall stack of manuscript pages,
squared up and tied with string, a pencil lying across the top. It has
not been touched in a long time; it is tidy and slightly sad. On the
right side, where someone has actually been working, is cheerful
disorder: a shoebox full of index cards, a few cards fanned out of it, an
open laptop whose screen shows only plain rows of gray lines, a mug, and
a single printed sheet with one line circled. Everything on the right is
turned slightly away from the stack, as if the work wandered off from it
on purpose. No people and no hands; the person has just stepped out.

The mood is dry and quietly funny, not wistful: a well-organized escape
from a job that was never finished. Restrained and observational, the way
a good cartoon is restrained.

Style: a painting, not a photograph and not a diagram. Ink and gray wash
on warm off-white paper, loose but precise, with plenty of untouched
paper showing.

Color: black ink and grays only, on the paper's own off-white. Exactly
one spot of color in the whole image: the circle drawn around the line on
the printed sheet, in orange (#E8740C). No other color anywhere: no
blue, no green, no brown, no warm-tinted grays.

No text of any kind. No letters, words, numbers, logos, signatures or
legible writing anywhere, including on the pages, the cards and the
screen: every page, card and screen shows only abstract gray lines.

Leave the top third of the image calm and nearly empty (open wall or
plain paper tone) and a quiet strip along the bottom, so a title and an
author's name can be set over them later. Keep the table and objects in
the middle.

Use your image generation tool to paint it. Save the finished image as art/cover.png in the current directory, creating the art directory if needed. Change nothing else in this directory.
I’ll use the imagegen skill to paint the cover, then save it as `art/cover.png` at the requested dimensions.
The painting is finished. I’m sizing the PNG to 1600 × 2560 pixels and saving it in `art/`.
